s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic eruption with skin lesions and liver dysfunction
salient_findings: Pruritic eruption that began on the trunk and spread to all extremities
Scleral icterus and multiple dusky, thin plaques with a central collarette of scale
Hyperkeratotic plaques and deeply seated vesicles with a greenish-black hue on hands and feet
key_facts: Eruption began on the trunk and spread to all extremities
Denied contact allergens, fever, or hyperhidrosis
No prior history of atopic dermatitis, dermatophytosis, or hand eczema
Punch biopsy of the right palm revealed psoriasiform epidermal acanthosis and intraepidermal spongiosis

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rosea
shortlist.why_kept: Punch biopsies of the chest and thigh were consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Primary biliary cirrhosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has pruritic eruption and liver dysfunction, which are common symptoms of this disease

shortlist.label: Porphyria cutanea tarda
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has liver dysfunction and skin lesions, which are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Alcoholic liver disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, which is a risk factor for this disease

shortlist.label: Autoimmune hepatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has liver dysfunction and skin lesions, which can be associated with autoimmune hepatitis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a pruritic eruption with dusky, thin plaques and hyperkeratotic plaques, especially on the hands and feet, along with the laboratory findings of elevated bilirubin and liver enzymes, and the biopsy results showing psoriasiform epidermal acanthosis and intraepidermal spongiosis, are consistent with porphyria cutanea tarda, which is often associated with liver disease, including alcoholic cirrhosis.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rosea
rejected.why: While the biopsy results from the chest and thigh are consistent with pityriasis rosea, the overall clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not support this as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Primary biliary cirrhosis
rejected.why: This condition primarily affects the bile ducts and is not typically associated with the skin findings described in the case.

rejected.label: Alcoholic liver disease
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, this diagnosis does not directly explain the skin manifestations.

rejected.label: Autoimmune hepatitis
rejected.why: The laboratory findings and clinical presentation do not specifically support autoimmune hepatitis as the primary diagnosis, especially given the presence of skin findings more characteristic of porphyria cutanea tarda.
